facts.statement: Abdarainurus is a genus of titanosaur dinosaur from the Alagteeg Formation in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Abdarainurus (meaning "Abdrant Nuru tail" after the holotype locality) is a genus of titanosaur dinosaur from the Alagteeg Formation in Mongolia.

facts.statement: The known remains of Abdarainurus consist of eight front tail vertebrae, one middle tail vertebra, and several chevrons.
facts.quote: Abdarainurus is not known from many remains; it is only known from eight front tail vertebrae and a middle tail vertebra and several chevrons.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PIN 5669/1 was discovered in 1970 in Abdrant Nuru during a Joint Soviet–Mongolian Paleontological expedition and excavated by V. P. Tverdokhlebov.
facts.quote: The holotype, PIN 5669/1, was discovered in 1970 in Abdrant Nuru, hence the genus name, during a Joint Soviet–Mongolian Paleontological expedition and was excavated by V. P. Tverdokhlebov of Saratov State University.

facts.statement: The species Abdarainurus barsboldi was formally named in February 2020.
facts.quote: The species Abdarainurus barsboldi was named in February 2020.

facts.statement: Abdarainurus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 85 million years ago in the Santonian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 85 millones de años, en el Santoniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Remains of Abdarainurus were found in the Alagteeg Formation in the northern part of the Gobi Desert in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados en la Formación Alagteeg en la parte norte del desierto de Gobi de Mongolia.

facts.statement: Abdarainurus coexisted with the ankylosaur Pinacosaurus sp., as well as indeterminate turtles and dinosaurs.
facts.quote: coexistió con el anquilosaurio Pinacosaurus sp., y tortugas y dinosaurios indeterminados.

facts.statement: Averianov and Lopatin suggested that Abdarainurus was most likely a basal titanosaur based on having the fewest unique features in their analysis.
facts.quote: As Abdarainurus was resolved with the fewest unique features as a basal titanosaur, Averianov and Lopatin suggested that phylogenetic result was the most likely, shown below.

facts.statement: The type species A. barsboldi was named in honor of the Mongolian paleontologist Rinchengin Barsbold and formally described in early 2020.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, A. barsboldi, fue nombrado en honor del paleontólogo mongol Rinchengin Barsbold y se describió formalmente a principios de 2020.

facts.statement: The genus name Abdarainurus means "Abdrant Nuru tail," derived from the Russian pronunciation of the locality Abdrant Nuru and the Greek word for tail.
facts.quote: El nombre del género fue puesto por el lugar donde se encontraron los restos, Abdrant Nuru, en la pronunciación rusa, Abdarain Nuru, y urus, del griego antiguo ουρά, "cola".

facts.statement: Abdarainurus fossils represent a fragmentary skeleton of tail vertebrae and haemal arches, possessing 16 unique and diagnostic anatomical features.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Abdarainurus representan una parte fragmentaria del esqueleto, vértebras de la cola y arcos hemales, con 16 características anatómicas únicas y diagnósticas.

facts.statement: The time range for Abdarainurus is estimated from 85.7 to 72.2 million years ago, spanning the Santonian to Campanian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The fossils were left unprepared until at least 2000, when paleontologist Andrei Podlesnow revealed that they probably belonged to a new genus of sauropod.
